# Refactor: decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` (1,132 lines)

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` — 1,132 lines.

## Problem statement

The worklist mouse-input test suite exceeds the 1,000-line maintainability
ceiling (~1,132 lines) and should be decomposed so that no test file exceeds the
ceiling.

## Goal

Break the test file into cohesive modules so no file exceeds 1,000 lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No file exceeds 1,000 lines.
2. All imports still resolve; all existing tests pass without modification to
   their assertions (move-only refactor).
3. No new circular imports.
4. All related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate test groups and update imports; do not change test
  assertions or test logic.
- **Test-file scope.** This item exists because the producer declined to include
  test-file decomposition in WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B (intake Q1 → answer A):
  "production modules only; tests stay unmodified as the behaviour gate and a
  follow-up item is filed for the two oversized suites."
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf test groups first.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B** — *Decompose packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts god class*
  (parent epic; discovered-from intake Q1 → answer A).

## Sequencing & validation (added at plan time, WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B)

- **Prerequisite:** `WL-0MVND6OOL004SK9N` (finalise the production barrel) — the
  production split must land first; splitting these tests against a moving
  barrel would churn imports twice.
- **Test-first gate:** the worklist split guard
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`, `WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J`)
  already asserts every production module ≤1,000 lines. Extend the same guard
  (or add a sibling guard) to assert every `worklist*.test.ts` file is ≤1,000
  lines once this item lands.
- **Move-only:** relocate describe blocks and their imports; assertions and test
  names stay byte-identical. Import from concrete `worklist.*.js` module paths
  only where the barrel does not expose an internal symbol — never from
  `index.ts`.
- **Validation:** `tsc --noEmit`/build, split guard green, and the full
  `packages/herdr` suite green (`/skill:test`).

# Decompose `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (4,284 lines)

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6 (Refactor: decompose
`packages/herdr/src/index.ts` god module).
**Status:** follow-up, deliberately **outside** that epic.

## Why this is not part of the index.ts epic

The index.ts split (WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6) is a move-only refactor whose
behaviour gate is that `index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts` and
`fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` stay **byte-identical**. Decomposing
`index.test.ts` inside the same epic would erase that signal, so it is filed
here as a separate item (plan decision Q3 → A).

## Target outcome

`packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (4,284 lines, measured 2026-11-05) is split
into cohesive test modules grouped by the production module they exercise
(commands, args, pane-capture, background, interactive/resolvers,
downtime-deps, settings/main) or another agreed grouping, with no test cases
lost and no production-code changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wc -l` reports ≤ 1,000 lines for every resulting `index*.test.ts` module.
- The total number of test cases (`it(`/`test(`) and assertions is unchanged before and after; no test is deleted, skipped or weakened.
- No production module changes; `packages/herdr` build and full test suite pass.
- Shared fixtures/helpers are extracted into a single helper module rather than duplicated across the new files.
- The split guard's line-ceiling gate excludes test files (asserted explicitly) so test sizes are not policed by the production ceiling.

## Baseline metrics (measured 2026-11-05 on `dev` @ 33bd3a07)

AC1/AC2 are verified against these numbers before and after the split:

- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — **4,284 lines**; 34 top-level
  `describe` blocks (41 including nested); **226 `it(...)` declarations** plus
  one `it.each` table with 4 parameterised cases (**231 executed cases**);
  **400 `expect(...)` assertions**; 4 `beforeEach`, 15 `afterEach`.
- No `it.skip`, `it.only` or `test(` call exists today; none may be added.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.split-guard.test.ts` — 484 lines (already under the
  ceiling and otherwise untouched apart from the AC5 assertion).

## Grouping map (inventory, measured 2026-11-05)

| Proposed module | Describes it takes (start line → length) | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `index.args.test.ts` | `buildSendToPiArgs` (72→103), `buildRunInPaneArgs` (175→100), item-tab anchor variants (275→43, 318→69), pane-id capture flag (3436→26), request priority (4005→24) | ~365 |
| `index.interactive.test.ts` | `extractWorkItemId` (387→17), `resolveInteractiveWorkspaceId` (404→30), `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` (434→116), `defaultInteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResolver` (550→93), `closeInteractiveTabRootPane` (643→123), `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority` (4111→86), operator-dispatch chain (4197→87) | ~552 |
| `index.commands.test.ts` | `stripCommandPrefix` (766→116), shortcuts.json routing (882→119), `routeCommand` (1001→56), `stripAgentPromptPrefix` (1057→48) | ~339 |
| `index.pane-capture.test.ts` | `parsePaneIdFile` (3462→17), `capturePaneIdFromFile` (3479→85) | ~128 |
| `index.background.test.ts` | `buildBackgroundLogPath` (3629→14), `spawnBackgroundShell` (3643→64), `formatBackgroundFailure` (3707→44), `spawnBackgroundPi` (3751→57), `spawnBackgroundPi` priority env (4029→82) | ~261 |
| `index.settings.test.ts` | `configureWorklogTarget` (1105→108) | ~108 |
| `index.downtime-deps*.test.ts` | `createDowntimeDeps` (1213→**1,407**), `host-wide audit admission` (2620→380), `recordDispatch` (3000→161), `recordError` (3161→37), `recordDispatchFailure` (3198→83), `getDueScheduledPrompt` (3281→89), `recordScheduledPromptTrigger` (3370→66), `rotation wiring` (3564→65) | ~2,288 |
| `index.stalled-work-wiring.test.ts` | `stalled-work production wiring` (3808→197) | ~197 |

Consequences of the inventory:

- The single `createDowntimeDeps` describe (**1,407 lines**) cannot move into one
  module under AC1. It must be subdivided by its nested describes (or at a
  shared-setup seam) so that the downtime-deps family lands in at least three
  modules ≤ 1,000 lines each, with `createDowntimeDeps` setup in
  `index.fixtures.ts`.
- The 2,288-line downtime-deps family is the bulk of the work; the remaining
  ~1,750 lines split cleanly by production module.

## Minimal implementation

1. Inventory done — see **Grouping map** above (verify it still matches before
   moving code; the file grows over time).
2. Extract shared mocks/fixtures to `packages/herdr/src/index.fixtures.ts`
   (suite-wide `beforeEach`/`afterEach` host-CPU pinning, `makeInteractiveAnchorDeps`,
   `loadInteractiveAnchorHelpers`, `createDowntimeDeps` stubs and other shared
   arrange helpers).
3. Move blocks into `index.<concern>.test.ts` files; keep imports pointing at
   `./index.js` (the barrel) so the public-surface contract keeps being tested.
   Import a concrete `./index.<slice>.js` path only where the barrel does not
   expose the symbol.
4. Add the explicit AC5 assertion to `index.split-guard.test.ts`: test/fixture
   files are excluded from the production line ceiling (today that exclusion is
   only implicit in `productionModules()` filtering).
5. Update `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/dispatcher-anchor-family.ts`
   `KNOWN_CONSUMER_FILES` (it names `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`, and
   `findBarrelConsumers(...)` is asserted to equal the list exactly) to name the
   module that keeps the `DispatcherAnchorDeps` type imports.
6. Verify with `/skill:test` scoped to `packages/herdr`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — source of the split (4,284 lines).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.*.test.ts` — new test modules.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.fixtures.ts` — shared fixtures (new).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.split-guard.test.ts` — receives the AC5 assertion.
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/dispatcher-anchor-family.ts` — frozen
  consumer list update (test tooling, not a production module).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate `describe` blocks, helpers and imports; test names and
  assertions stay byte-identical. No test deleted, skipped, renamed or weakened.
- **Test-only change;** must not alter production behaviour or public surface.
  `packages/herdr/src/index.split-baseline.json` is a frozen contract — never
  regenerate it to make a gate green.
- **Fixture naming matters.** `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`'s
  `isTestOrFixture()` recognises only `*.test.ts` and `*.fixtures.ts`, while
  `INDEX_FAMILY_PATTERN` (`/^index(\.[\w-]+)?\.ts$/`) *does* match
  `index.test-helpers.ts` — so a helper named `index.test-helpers.ts` would be
  treated as an index-family **production** module and held to the 1,000-line
  ceiling plus the single-declaration/single-callsite gates. Use
  `index.fixtures.ts`, matching the existing `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` /
  `host-dispatch-budget.fixtures.ts` convention.
- **Do not pollute the production size gate.** `INDEX_SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` and
  `INDEX_SPLIT_ALLOWLIST_CEILING` are `['index.ts']` and shrink-only; no split
  test module may be added to them.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf test groups first, keeping the
  tree green between moves; run the scoped suite after each module.
- **Guard divergence is deliberate.** The sibling test-decomposition items
  (`WL-0MVHURHZI000CS5L`, `WL-0MVHUU096008OQSW`) extend their split guard to
  *police* `worklist*.test.ts` at ≤1,000 lines; this item's AC5 requires the
  opposite for the index family (test files explicitly **excluded** from the
  production ceiling). Do not harmonise the two.
- **No production-split prerequisite.** `index.ts` is still 2,072 lines and
  remains on the shrink-only allowlist; its epic (WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6) is
  deleted, so this item is independent. Moves must not touch `index.ts` itself.

## Related work

- WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6 — parent epic (deleted; the split shipped as separate
  production modules and `index.ts` remains on the allowlist).
- WL-0MVHURHZI000CS5L — decompose `worklist.test.ts` (7,073 lines), blocked.
- WL-0MVHUU096008OQSW — decompose `worklist-mouse.test.ts` (1,132 lines), blocked.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.split-guard.test.ts` / `index.split-baseline.json` —
  the structural gates that must stay green.

## Appendix: planning questions, findings and answers

**Duplicate check.** `wl search "index.test.ts"`,
`wl search "decompose test god file split module herdr"` and
`wl search "index.test.ts decompose split test"` performed 2026-11-05. The only
overlapping items are the sibling *worklist* test decompositions (different
files, no AC overlap) and this item; no completed item satisfies these ACs.
**No overlapping completed item found** — proceed.

- **Q: Is `index.test-helpers.ts` (named in the original Key Files) a safe
  fixture name?** Answer (plan, verified against
  `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/{scan,index-family}.ts` with `tsx`):
  **no** — it matches `INDEX_FAMILY_PATTERN` and is not recognised by
  `isTestOrFixture()`, so it would be gated as production. Accepted naming:
  `index.fixtures.ts`. Evidence: `INDEX_FAMILY_PATTERN.test('index.test-helpers.ts') === true`,
  `isTestOrFixture('index.test-helpers.ts') === false`.
- **Q: Does the line-count in the title/description still hold?** Answer
  (measured): no — the file is 4,284 lines, not 3,990. Title and description
  corrected; counts recorded under **Baseline metrics**.
- **Q: Does the item stay clear of the frozen production gates?** Answer
  (verified): yes, provided the split does not add test modules to the
  allowlist, does not regenerate `index.split-baseline.json`, and updates the
  *test-tooling* `KNOWN_CONSUMER_FILES` list, which currently names
  `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` and is asserted by exact equality.
- **Q: Is `claim` a real group in this file (the original description listed
  it)?** Answer (inventory): no — `claim` coverage lives in `claim.test.ts`;
  removed from the grouping list.
- **Decision (scope sizing / phasing):** no children are created and no
  phasing is needed — this is a single move-only deliverable. If the 1,407-line
  `createDowntimeDeps` describe proves unmanageable during implementation,
  `implement` may create children then, test-first (AC5 assertion → fixture
  module → downtime-deps sub-split → remaining concerns).
- **Decision (residual barrel test file):** `index.test.ts` is expected to be
  removed once its describes are distributed; the public-surface contract is
  preserved by the split-guard baseline and by the new modules importing
  `./index.js`. A thin residual `index.test.ts` is acceptable if a home is
  needed for file-level setup.
- **Note (effort/risk provenance):** the autoplan pre-check ran
  `effort-and-risk` with its zeroed placeholder payload (`o=m=p=0`) and wrote
  `Extra Small`/`Low`; step 8 replaced both fields with a real three-point
  estimate (see the effort/risk fields and the `effort_and_risk_skill`
  comment).

# Canonical full suite excludes `packages/` tests (tui 30 + shared 13 files)

*Discovered from WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR (canonical suite root-level `tests/` coverage).* That item closed the `tests/` gap by replacing the two narrow `suiteCommands` with the umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`. It deliberately kept its scope to `tests/`, so the `packages/` gap remains.

**Note:** file counts have grown since the work item was created — `packages/tui` now has 30 test files (was 22) and `packages/shared` has 13 (was 12). The `packages/herdr` count is 129, unchanged. Repository total: 453 test files (up from 440).

## Problem Statement

`.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` (the single source of full-suite evidence for `/skill:test --type full`, the ship release gate and audit F3) resolves only to `tests/`. Tracked test files by location:

| Location | Test files | In canonical suite? |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/` | 277 | Yes (since WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR) |
| `packages/herdr` | 129 | No — producer decision (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); opt-in `--type herdr` / `--group herdr` |
| `packages/tui` | 30 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| `packages/shared` | 13 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| **Repository total** | **453** | **277** |

`packages/tui/**/*.test.ts` (30 files, all under `packages/tui/extensions/`) and `packages/shared/**/*.test.ts` (13 files) run under a bare `npx vitest` / CI but are referenced by neither `suiteCommands` nor any cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths, so no gate can execute or cache-evidence them. (Note: a `tui-extensions` group exists in `groups` but is not wired into `suiteCommands`.)

## Goal

Every `packages/` test file is either executed by the canonical full suite (or a cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths), or has an explicit documented exclusion with a rationale — the same standard WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR applied to `tests/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.pi/test-config.json` covers `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` tests (in `suiteCommands`, or as named `groups` entries wired to their paths so `implement.py finish` selects them), or each exclusion is documented with a rationale in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`.
- A full `/skill:test` run (`python3 <test-skill>/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --json`) reports the newly covered files as executed, with the executed-file count recorded in the work item.
- Any failures surfaced by the change are triaged into `test-failure` work items.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (the "Test gates" section is shared, not duplicated) carries the updated coverage table (files executed / excluded / why) and the measured runtime.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Evidence-path constraint:** full-suite evidence for the audit resolves `--type full` from `suiteCommands` only; a new `groups.*` entry alone does not satisfy a "full suite passes" AC (see `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` → "Cache evidence scope").
- **Vitest filters are substring matches** on the repository-relative path, so `packages/shared` / `packages/tui` can be selected by positional filters (`-- tests` umbrella does not cover them; `-- packages` would also pull in `packages/herdr`, which is excluded by producer decision).
- **Do not re-litigate the herdr decision** (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix; `groups.herdr` added by WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN).
- Measure runtime before/after with the test-skill runner (`run_tests.py`), not ad-hoc `npx vitest`.
- Beware the `run_tests.py --suite node` trap: that suite name resolves through the legacy convention path (`tests/{unit,node,cli}`) and ignores `suiteCommands`; use the default `--suite all` for canonical runs.

## Existing state

The canonical suite is a single command: `npm --silent test -- tests` (277 files, ~791 s vitest duration, ~1065 s wall clock). The `tui-extensions` group exists in `groups` but is not wired into `suiteCommands`. There is no group for `packages/shared`.

## Desired change

Add `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` to the canonical full suite coverage. The simplest approach is to add additional commands to `suiteCommands`:

```jsonc
{
  "suiteCommands": [
    "npm --silent test -- tests",
    "npm --silent test -- packages/shared",
    "npm --silent test -- packages/tui/extensions"
  ]
}
```

This adds two positional filters that are precise: `packages/shared` matches only the 13 shared test files, and `packages/tui/extensions` matches only the 30 tui test files (all under `extensions/`), neither of which would match `packages/herdr`.

Alternatively, create named groups (`shared`, `tui`) and wire them into `suiteCommands` as separate commands — same effect, but with changed-scope selection benefits.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/test-config.json` — add `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` to `suiteCommands` (or create named groups + wire them)
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — update the coverage table and runtime section
- `vitest.config.ts` — no change expected; existing config handles `packages/` correctly

## Related work

- **WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR** — closed the `tests/` coverage gap (umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`); records the OPEN QUESTION that became this item.
- **WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8** — herdr package suite excluded by producer decision (won't-fix).
- **WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN** — added `groups.herdr` to `.pi/test-config.json`.
- **WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1** — source of the additional-gap evidence for `packages/tui/extensions/**`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should packages/herdr be included?" — Answer (work item description): No — producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix. Source: work item description.
- Q: "What about the `tui-extensions` group that already exists?" — Answer: It is not wired into `suiteCommands`, so it provides no full-suite gate coverage. The brief proposes wiring it (or creating an equivalent group) into suiteCommands. Source: inspection of `.pi/test-config.json`.
- Q: "File counts have changed since the work item was created — should we update the title?" — Answer: Yes — the title should be updated to reflect current counts (30 + 13, not 22 + 12). Source: `git ls-files` on current tree.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Runtime increase (medium).** Adding 43 files to the canonical suite increases wall-clock. *Mitigation:* measure before/after with `run_tests.py`; `timeoutPerCommand` is 3600 s, so there is headroom.
- **New coverage may surface pre-existing failures (medium).** Neither `packages/tui` nor `packages/shared` has run under the canonical gate, so latent failures could appear. *Mitigation:* triage into `test-failure` items (AC3).
- **Filter precision (low).** `packages/shared` and `packages/tui/extensions` are substring filters; verified against `git ls-files` that they match only the intended 13 + 30 files and not `packages/herdr`. *Assumption:* `packages/tui` has no test files outside `extensions/` (confirmed: 30/30 are under `extensions/`).
- **Scope creep (low).** `packages/herdr` is explicitly out of scope (producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); covering it would require re-litigating a closed won't-fix decision. Any further gap (e.g. a new package) becomes a linked work item, not added scope.
- **Assumption:** adding commands to `suiteCommands` (rather than only `groups`) is required, because `--type full` evidence resolves from `suiteCommands` only (evidence-path constraint). A group-only change would not satisfy AC2.

# Make groupings stable

## Problem statement

When the herdr selection list re-sorts on refresh, items sometimes move from
one group to another even though nothing about them changed materially. This
causes disconcerting movement in the list. The list should only change when
the underlying items change in a material way (e.g. a new key file is added,
or the priority changes). Additionally, items should sort in priority order —
all high items ahead of medium, all medium ahead of low.

## Users

- **Herdr users / producers** who watch the worklist to decide what to work
  on next. A stable list lets them track where work sits; gratuitous movement
  breaks their mental model of the queue.
- **Producers reviewing the in-review queue** who rely on a predictable
  within-group order to find the most important work first.

User story: *As a Herdr user, I want the worklist grouping and ordering to be
a stable function of the items themselves, so that an item only changes
group when its content (key files, priority, stage/status) or the item set
changes — and within each group, high-priority items always rank above
medium, which rank above low.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Group assignment is **content-deterministic**: for a fixed set of items
      with fixed key files / priority / stage / status, the group each item
      lands in is identical regardless of the order in which the items are
      presented to the grouping algorithm (canonical ordering applied before
      the greedy first-fit packing). A transient change such as an
      `updatedAt` timestamp (comment added, audit run) must never change an
      item's group.
- [ ] An item's group membership changes **only** when a material input
      changes: its key files section, its priority, its stage/status, or the
      item set itself (item added/removed). Verified by a stability test
      that perturbs non-material inputs (`updatedAt`, input order) and
      asserts group labels/numbers are unchanged.
- [ ] Within each group (Critical Group N and Group N), items sort by
      **priority first (high → medium → low)**, then by the existing stage
      sub-order (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining), then by
      id — so all high items appear ahead of all medium items, which appear
      ahead of all low items. The `in_review` 6-bucket comparator already
      sorts priority-first and keeps that behaviour.
- [ ] The change is applied **and kept in sync** in both mirrors: core
      `wl next` / `wl worklist` grouping (`src/commands/grouping.ts`,
      `src/worklist-selection.ts`) and the herdr plugin copy
      (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`); shared grouping tests cover both
      copies.
- [ ] `wl next -n N` and the herdr worklist still emit the canonical section
      order (Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review) with no
      regression in existing grouping/smart-selection behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
      comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Greedy first-fit file-path conflict detection is retained — the change
  makes it order-independent, it does not replace the packing strategy.
- Herdr plugin has zero npm dependencies and cannot import from
  `src/commands/`; the mirror must stay a self-contained pure duplication
  (per WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B decision Q2c).
- The always-show-mandatory guarantee of `selectWorkItems`
  (`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`) is preserved — grouping only
  reorders and stamps, never filters or drops items.
- Default `maxGroups` of 3 for file-path-based groups is unchanged.

## Existing state

- `regroupWorkItems` (herdr) / `selectBrowseFeed` (core) recompute group
  assignments on every refresh from the merged selection.
- `groupItemsByFilePaths` is a greedy first-fit over items **in input
  order**; the input order fluctuates with `updatedAt` (comment/audit
  churn), so the same item set can pack into different groups across
  refreshes. That is the root cause of the observed group hopping.
- Within-group ordering (`compareGroupableItems`) currently sorts by stage
  sub-order first (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining), then
  priority; `in_review` items already sort priority-first.

## Desired change

1. Make `groupItemsByFilePaths` (and hence `assignItemGroups`) a pure
   function of the item content: sort/canonicalise the input items by a
   stable content-derived key before greedy packing, so group membership
   depends only on ids, key files, priority and stage/status — not on
   transient ordering.
2. Make priority the **primary** within-group sort key in
   `compareGroupableItems` (both mirrors), keeping the stage sub-order as
   the secondary key.
3. Keep the two mirrors in sync and extend the grouping tests in both
   locations with stability assertions (order perturbation + non-material
   input perturbation must not change group membership or ordering).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — core `groupItemsByFilePaths` / `assignItemGroups` / `compareGroupableItems`; canonicalise input order; priority-first within-group sort.
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — core `selectBrowseFeed` grouping pipeline consuming `assignItemGroups`.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — mirrored plugin copy of the same algorithm; must stay in sync.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems`; input order source feeding `regroupWorkItems` (contract only — no functional change expected unless needed for canonicalisation).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — callers of `regroupWorkItems`.
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — core grouping tests; add stability assertions.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — plugin grouping tests; mirror stability assertions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Within-group order change is intentional but observable:** making priority
  the primary within-group sort key changes which item of a group renders
  first (stage sub-order becomes secondary). Existing tests in
  `grouping.test.ts` / `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` that assert the old
  stage-first order must be updated deliberately, not incidentally.
- **Canonicalisation key must be content-derived:** the pre-pack sort key

# Redirect post-push verification full-suite runs to a pinned isolated worktree

## Problem Statement

A full-suite run executed from the main checkout during post-push verification
can race with a sibling `implement.py finish` fast-forwarding the main
checkout's local `dev` (`git merge --ff-only`), swapping source files mid-run
and producing phantom failures (WL-0MVSLXT79008D4X6 evidence: 4 failures in
`tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` / `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` at
1abe9618; identical tree green in an isolated worktree minutes earlier).

## Goal (User Story)

As an AI agent running `implement.py finish`, I want post-push verification and
audit cache-miss full-suite runs to execute in an isolated worktree pinned to
the pushed commit — never live in the main checkout — so a sibling finish
fast-forwarding `dev` cannot swap the files a suite is reading.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mitigate the race:** the post-push verification path is updated so that
   full-suite runs execute in an isolated worktree against a pinned commit,
   and the cache entry is grafted into the main checkout — not run live in
   the main checkout where a sibling finish can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
2. The post-push verification path (and the audit skill F3 cache-miss
   auto-execution path) resolves an isolated worktree for the commit being
   verified and executes the full suite there — not in the live main checkout
   where a sibling `finish` can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
3. The fresh cache entry produced by the isolated-worktree run is grafted into
   the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` before/mirroring the pre-push hook's
   `mirror_suite_cache` semantics (never overwrites an existing entry), so
   read-only post-push verification and audits serve the grafted entry.
4. The mitigation is minimal and localised: document + redirect test execution
   to worktrees; it does not rewrite the post-push verification pipeline or
   change verdict semantics (`green`/`red`/`missing`/`not_applicable`).
5. The single-owner main-checkout flock lock (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84) and the
   main-checkout guard (WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O) remain intact; finish refuses
   loudly rather than masking a real failure.
6. The full project test suite passes with the change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish()` read-only
  verification step and Step-6 main-checkout dev fast-forward
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_run_tests_via_test_skill` /
  F3 auto-execution (`run_cached(..., cwd=per_audit_root)`)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py` — suite execution
  and cache
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — guidance to match

## Constraints

- Must not break the dev-push pre-push hook's cache mirroring
  (`mirror_suite_cache`, `src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` in ContextHub /
  `.githooks/pre-push`).
- The audit skill's F3 cache-miss path must be covered (audits running in the
  main checkout face the same race).
- Worktree creation cost is assumed negligible (node_modules is symlinked);
  latency must stay bounded.
- Implementation repo: framework skills live in the SorraAgents repo
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`); run
  `wl` worktree-safely with `--worklog-dir` when operating there.

# Suppress known phantom test-failure patterns in triage

## Problem Statement

When the main checkout's `dev` is fast-forwarded mid-test-run by a sibling
`implement.py finish`, a suite produces failures that exist in **no single
commit** (tests from X, source from Y). The test-failure triage logic can mint
phantom `test-failure` work items from such mixed-tree output, creating noise
and false work for producers (WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET).

## Goal (User Story)

As a producer, I want the triage logic to detect and suppress known phantom
patterns (mixed-tree verdicts from a moving checkout) so they no longer
auto-mint critical `test-failure` work items, while genuine failures still
triage normally.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No phantom test-failure items:** after the mitigation, the race no longer
   generates additional phantom test-failure work items without manual triage;
   existing test-failure triage logic detects and suppresses known phantom
   patterns.
2. The test-failure triage helper detects known phantom signatures — a
   `state_changed_during_run` / mid-run fast-forward flag, or output recorded
   while the executing checkout was not a stable, pinned tree — and suppresses
   auto-creation of a `test-failure` work item, recording the suppression
   reason instead.
3. A suppressed phantom is still reported in the run's output/report with an
   explicit notice (`state_changed_during_run` notice code or equivalent),
   so the information is never silently lost — it is simply not minted as a
   critical item.
4. A genuine failure on a stable checkout still creates/updates a
   `test-failure` work item exactly as before (no behaviour change for real
   failures).
5. The suppression is covered by tests (both a phantom pattern that is
   suppressed and a genuine failure that is triaged).

# Regression guard: `wl update --audit-text` survives a drifted-but-repairable DB

discovered-from:AH-0MW4W2CAJ000NUJZ

## Context

The 2026-11-06 AI_Hell release run surfaced an audit-persistence failure: the
ship audit gate's `wl update --audit-text` exited rc=1 while the AI_Hell
worklog database was drifted (`schemaVersion=8` vs the installed tool's
`9`), so neither the assembled audit report nor the compact fallback notice
could be persisted. The current build heals such a database on connect
(`REQUIRED_COLUMNS` in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`), and a
unit-level repair test already exists
(`packages/shared/src/audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts`, WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV).
That test calls `saveAuditResult()` directly, so it does **not** prove the
production path — the `wl update --audit-text` **command** — still works
against a drifted database. A regression that broke the command (or bypassed
the store's repair) would leave that guard green.

## User story

As a release producer, I want a deterministic test that drives the real
`wl update --audit-text` command against a drifted-but-repairable worklog
database, so a future change cannot silently reintroduce the 2026-11-06
audit-persistence failure.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A test in the ContextHub `wl` suite (`tests/cli/update-audit-text-schema-drift.test.ts`)
   proves that `wl update --audit-text` succeeds (rc=0, `success: true`)
   against a temp-DB fixture drifted to `schemaVersion=8` with the
   `audit_results.fingerprint` column dropped and its
   `audit_fingerprint_added` metadata sentinel removed.
2. The test asserts the write actually landed: the `audit_results` row exists
   for the item with the expected summary and a non-null fingerprint, and the
   connect-time repair restored the `fingerprint` column plus its sentinel.
3. The test is deterministic and self-contained: temp directory
   (`createTempDir`/`enterTempDir` pattern), direct SQLite drift on that copy
   only, no live `wl`/`network`/`pi` calls.
4. A second test exercises the audit-skill persist sequence (`wl audit-set`
   then `wl update --audit-text`) against a drifted database and asserts both
   succeed, so the release-gate path end to end is covered.
5. The test fails against a build with the connect-time repair disabled and
   passes with it (red/green witness recorded on AH-0MW4W2CAJ000NUJZ).
6. `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` documents that the connect-time repair keeps the
   audit-write command working on a drifted database and names the regression
   test that locks it in.
7. The full ContextHub `wl` suite passes.

## Constraints

- Test-only change plus documentation; no production behaviour change is
  intended. The connect-time repair is treated as intended drift-resilience
  (recorded assumption on AH-0MW4W2CAJ000NUJZ).
- Deterministic only: no live AI_Hell/ContextHub worklog mutation, no
  network, no `pi` invocation.
- Do not bump `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` or change migration semantics.

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/update-audit-text-schema-drift.test.ts` (new)
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` (helpers used as-is)
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` (`REQUIRED_COLUMNS` behaviour under test)
- `src/commands/update.ts` (`--audit-text` write path)
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` (`wl audit-set`)
- `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` (docs)

- AH-0MW4W2CAJ000NUJZ — parent tracker in AI_Hell (this item is its mirror)
- WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV — additive schema repair + unit-level repair test
- WL-0MW1W61CG005K893 — migration fix basis (schemaVersion advance on zero pending)

# Inconsistent soft-delete predicate: `wl list` excludes only `status=deleted` while `wl update` rejects any non-empty `deletedBy`

## Problem statement

Two code paths disagree about what counts as "soft-deleted":

- **`wl list`** excludes a row only when `status === 'deleted'` (`src/commands/list.ts`, the `includeDeleted` filter). It ignores `deletedBy`.
- **`wl update`** refuses to mutate a row whenever `deletedBy` is non-empty, regardless of `status` (`src/commands/update.ts`, the soft-delete guard `SA-0MUJBLZC60085DI9 AC1`, error code `deleted-item`). It ignores `status`.

The result is a row that is *both* visible and immutable:

- **visible** in `wl list --stage <X>` because its `status` is not `'deleted'`, and
- **immutable** because its `deletedBy` is set, so `wl update` rejects it as `deleted-item`.

## Impact

A soft-deleted-then-repaired item (e.g. `status=completed` with `deletedBy` retained to preserve deletion intent) that also carries `stage=in_review` shows up as a **release candidate** for `wl list --stage in_review`, but the audit runner's `wl update --status in_progress` fails with `deleted-item`. This blocks the `dev -> main` release gate (ship skill) for a row that is, by the CLI's own definition, deleted. It surfaced during the ship release attempt on 2026-11-06 (see MS-0MW22TQS8008021W), where four items had to be hand-repaired to clear `in_review` from the candidate list.

## Root cause

The two predicates are not derived from one shared definition of "soft-deleted":

| Path | Predicate | File / symbol |
|------|-----------|---------------|
| list | `item.status !== 'deleted'` | `src/commands/list.ts` — `includeDeleted` filter |
| update | `String(item.deletedBy ?? '').trim() !== ''` | `src/commands/update.ts` — soft-delete guard |

## Reproduction

1. Take a work item with `status=completed`, `stage=in_review`, and a non-empty `deletedBy` (e.g. any item repaired after a `wl delete`).
2. `wl list --stage in_review --json` → the item is returned as a candidate.
3. `wl update <id> --status in_progress --json` → `{ "success": false, "error": "deleted-item" }`.

Live evidence (tce-main-street store, 2026-11-08): the four items repaired during the ship run all have `status=completed`, `deletedBy=250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `stage=done`:

- `wl list --stage done --json` returns all four.
- `wl update MS-0MT3JK16W006A66P --title probe --json` returns `success:false, error:"deleted-item"`.

If their `stage` had remained `in_review`, they would have blocked the release gate exactly as described in the ship comment.

## Desired change

Define "soft-deleted" once and use it consistently. Either:

- **Option A (preferred):** treat a row as excluded/deleted whenever `status === 'deleted'` **or** `deletedBy` is non-empty, in `wl list` (and any other read path that projects "live" items). This makes visible rows always mutable.
- **Option B:** have the `wl update` soft-delete guard key on `status === 'deleted'` only, and treat `deletedBy` as pure attribution for non-deleted rows.

The chosen option must be applied to **every** read/selection path that can feed the release gate (`wl list --stage`, `wl worklist`, `wl next`), not just `wl list`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A single shared predicate function defines "soft-deleted" for both read and write paths.
- [ ] AC2: A row with non-empty `deletedBy` is either excluded from every list/selection path **or** is mutable via `wl update` — the two paths must agree (no visible-but-immutable rows).
- [ ] AC3: Regression test: an item with `status !== 'deleted'` but non-empty `deletedBy` has consistent treatment — if it is returned by `wl list --stage in_review`, `wl update` must accept a mutation on it; if it is excluded, `wl list` must not return it.
- [ ] AC4: Regression test: `wl list --stage in_review` never returns a row the release gate cannot audit (i.e. never a row for which `wl update --status in_progress` fails with `deleted-item`).
- [ ] AC5: `wl doctor` reports no findings introduced by the change; existing soft-deleted rows remain excluded from normal lists.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/list.ts` — `includeDeleted` filter (list-side predicate).
- `src/commands/update.ts` — soft-delete guard (`SA-0MUJBLZC60085DI9`), `deleted-item` error.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — consolidated read path consumed by selection lists.
- `src/commands/next.ts` — dispatch selection path.
- `src/commands/delete.ts` — sets `deletedBy` / `status=deleted`.
- `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` — status/stage validation.

## Related work

- **WL-0MLB703EH1FNOQR1** — "Exlude deleted from list" (completed). Covers only `status === 'deleted'`; this item covers the `deletedBy` dimension it left out. Its fix commit added no tests.
- **WL-0MV2E2ZS5001RGLO** — `wl delete` lost-update / soft-delete convergence.
- **WL-0MTFNIRXU007X7U4** — delete-side protection: unattributed deletes never override live items.
- **MS-0MW22TQS8008021W** (separate project) — residual `wl doctor` findings; the ship-comment symptom that exposed this mismatch.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `deletedBy` is intended as the authoritative soft-delete marker (per `SA-0MUJBLZC60085DI9`), so Option A is the safer reconciliation for read paths.
- **Risk — data semantics:** changing read-path visibility affects Herdr/TUI selection lists; the change must be rolled out with the shared predicate and its tests.
- **Risk — scope:** do not alter deletion attribution or merge/sync protection logic; only reconcile the predicate.

# Intake Brief: Fix `wl delete` deleteReason overwrite and add `--reason` flag

## Problem statement

`wl delete` unconditionally overwrites any existing `deleteReason` with the hardcoded string `"deleted via wl delete"` and offers no `--reason` flag. This destroys audit trails (operators who pre-set reasons lose them on delete) and defeats the delete-side merge protection introduced by WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO, because every CLI delete becomes "attributed" by a fabricated constant that cannot distinguish intent from absence of intent.

## Users

- **Bulk-cleanup operators**: agents or humans retiring stale backlog items who need each deletion to carry its specific rationale.
- **Merge-layer consumers**: the sync merge gate (`isAttributedDelete()`) that relies on `deleteReason` as a consent signal.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`wl delete` accepts `--reason <text>`** and stores it as `deleteReason`; the applied reason is echoed per id in `--json` output.
2. **When `--reason` is omitted, a pre-existing non-empty `deleteReason` is preserved.** The CLI must not pass a reason value that shadows the item's existing one — the `|| item.deleteReason` fallback in the database layer must become reachable.
3. **The default `"deleted via wl delete"` is applied only when no reason was supplied and the item has none already.** Crucially, this default must not, on its own, satisfy `isAttributedDelete()` from `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts:113`. The implementer decides: either the default is stored as empty (discarded for merge-gate purposes), or `isAttributedDelete()` is updated to exclude the CLI default string. Decision recorded in the implementation commit.
4. **Recursive deletion attributes each descendant distinctly** — at minimum the supplied (or preserved) reason plus the cascade source id — so a swept child is distinguishable from a deliberately retired item. Parent and descendants are reported separately in `--json` output.
5. **Tests cover:** (a) reason via `--reason` stored verbatim; (b) a pre-set reason survives delete with no `--reason`; (c) default applied only when item has none; (d) cascade records cascade source per descendant; (e) an unattributed CLI delete is **not** reported as an attributed delete (regression test for the merge gate).
6. **`wl update --delete-reason` on already-deleted items continues to work** as the documented repair path.

## Impact

Operators can record why an item was retired at the point of deletion, so bulk cleanups stay auditable and an accidental or intent-less delete can no longer masquerade as a deliberate one during a cross-agent sync merge.

## Constraints

- Must not break existing CLI consumers (JSON output contract, single-id legacy fields, batch semantics).
- Must not change the REST API's `deleted via API` default.
- The fix in `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` (the `|| item.deleteReason` fallback) must remain backward-compatible with API callers and any internal callers.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — hardcoded reason at line 82; add `--reason` option
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts:422-423` — `|| item.deleteReason` fallback (needs to become reachable)
- `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts:113` — `isAttributedDelete()` (may need updating per AC3 decision)
- `tests/cli/delete-batch.test.ts` — test home for AC1-5
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` — ensure new flags don't affect auto-sync

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO** (completed) — Delete-side protection: the merge gate this defect defeats.
- **WL-0MVZ5Y0VR0065TPJ** (open, plan_complete) — Add `--deleted-by` and `--delete-reason` flags (CLI parity with REST API). Subsumed by this critical bug. Recommend closing once this item is scheduled.
- **WL-0MTFNIRXU007X7U4** (completed) — Delete-side protection implementation.
- **WL-0MU38HN2J008WWTB** (completed) — Repair path via `wl update --delete-reason`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** The `--deleted-by` flag work from WL-0MVZ5Y0VR0065TPJ overlaps. If that item is not closed, it can become a child of this bug (or be folded into it). Decision: record as a decision in implementation.
- **Merge-gate regression:** Changing how `isAttributedDelete()` evaluates the default string could affect sync behaviour. A regression test must be written.
- **Backward compatibility:** Internal callers (API, other commands) may pass `deleteReason` explicitly. The fallback chain `opts?.deleteReason || item.deleteReason || ''` must handle `undefined`, `''`, and non-empty values correctly for all callers.
- **Assumption:** The `isAttributedDelete()` decision (AC3) should favour keeping the merge gate conservative — an unreasoned delete should not be treated as deliberate. The implementer should record the rationale in-code.

## Existing State

```
src/commands/delete.ts:82: const deleteReason = 'deleted via wl delete';
packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts:423: deleteReason: opts?.deleteReason || item.deleteReason || ''
```

Every `wl delete` invocation passes a non-empty literal, so the `|| item.deleteReason` fallback is never reached from the CLI. 216 of 847 deletions in the SA store carry the identical generic string, making them unauditable.

## Desired Change

- Add `--reason <text>` option to `wl delete`.
- When `--reason` is absent, do not pass a reason to the database layer so the existing `deleteReason` fallback kicks in.
- When both are absent, either store empty (merge-gate neutral) or a marker that `isAttributedDelete()` recognises as unattributed.
- Recursive deletes record cascade source per descendant.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was required: the seed context supplied a complete problem definition, reproduction evidence, six testable acceptance criteria, impact analysis, key files and related work, so the intake proceeded on the existing content (idempotent — re-running intake reproduces this same result without duplicating entries).

- Q: (none) — seed context sufficed to draft a clear brief; no producer questions were asked.
- Accepted design preference recorded from the description (AC3): the `isAttributedDelete()` decision (discard the default in favour of an empty reason, **or** stop counting the CLI default as intent) is deferred to implementation time and must be recorded in the implementation commit. No producer input needed to draft the brief; the implementer records the rationale.
- OPEN DECISION (non-blocking, for the producer at scheduling): `WL-0MVZ5Y0VR0065TPJ` (`wl delete: add --deleted-by and --delete-reason flags`) is the medium-priority predecessor of this critical superset. It should be folded into this item (closed as subsumed) once this item is scheduled, so the merge-gate regression test is written once. Recorded here so the decision is not lost; does not block intake completion.
## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-08T18:40Z** — Plan decomposition: created 4 child tasks (TEST, CLI, DB, VERIFY) covering all 6 parent ACs in test-first dependency order. Effort: Extra Small. Risk: Low.
- **2026-11-08T18:40Z** — Automated review: all 6 stages passed. AC coverage: all 6 parent ACs covered.

Add --reason <text> option to the wl delete CLI command.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **wl delete accepts --reason <text>**: The CLI adds an --reason option that accepts a freeform text string. The option is positional: `wl delete <id> --reason "cleaning up stale items"`.
2. **Reason stored as deleteReason**: The provided reason is passed through the call chain to the database layer and stored as the item deleteReason.
3. **No reason supplied, no default passed**: When --reason is absent, the CLI must NOT pass any deleteReason value to the database layer. The existing fallback in the DB layer (`|| item.deleteReason`) becomes reachable, preserving any pre-set reason.
4. **Reason echoed in --json output**: When deleting with --reason, the applied reason appears in the JSON output per-id results.
5. **Backward compatible JSON output**: The existing JSON output contract is preserved — single-id legacy fields remain, batch summary is additive.
6. **Backward compatible CLI**: Existing invocations without --reason continue to work as expected (the hardcoded default is removed; the DB fallback preserves existing reasons or stores empty).

## Implementation Notes

- Add the --reason option in `src/commands/delete.ts` after the existing --no-recursive and --no-sync options.
- Replace the hardcoded `const deleteReason = 'deleted via wl delete'` with logic that uses `options.reason` when provided, otherwise `undefined`.
- Pass the reason through to `db.delete(idLookup, recursive, { deletedBy, deleteReason })` — only when --reason was explicitly supplied, otherwise pass undefined so DB fallback reaches the item's existing deleteReason.
- The --reason value should be optional and non-empty. Reject empty strings with a validation error.

1. **Cascade source in descendant deleteReason**: When recursively deleting a parent item, each descendant's deleteReason must include the cascade source (parent id). Format: `cascade from <parent-id>: <reason or preserved reason>`.

# Create shared isSoftDeleted predicate in @worklog/shared

## Goal

Define a single, exported `isSoftDeleted(item: WorkItem): boolean` predicate function in the shared package that determines whether a work item is soft-deleted.

## Definition

A work item is soft-deleted when:
- `status === 'deleted'` **OR**
- `deletedBy` is non-empty (truthy after trim)

This matches the current `wl update` soft-delete guard logic while also including the `status` dimension.

**Do not conflate with existing related-but-distinct predicates:**
- `isAttributedDelete` in `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts` — delete *attribution* for merge protection, not visibility.
- `isDeleteIntent`/`Boolean(item.deletedBy) || Boolean(item.deleteReason)` in `src/claim-hold.ts` — claim-hold suppression.

Only the read/select/mutability predicate named in this epic is reconciled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC0 (parent AC1): A single shared predicate function defines "soft-deleted" for both read and write paths.
- [ ] AC1: `isSoftDeleted` is exported from `@worklog/shared` and importable by both `src/commands/list.ts` and `src/commands/update.ts`.
- [ ] AC2: `isSoftDeleted({ status: 'deleted', deletedBy: '' })` returns `true`.
- [ ] AC3: `isSoftDeleted({ status: 'completed', deletedBy: 'user@example.com' })` returns `true`.
- [ ] AC4: `isSoftDeleted({ status: 'completed', deletedBy: '' })` returns `false`.
- [ ] AC5: `isSoftDeleted({ status: 'open', deletedBy: '' })` returns `false`.
- [ ] AC6: Unit tests cover all four quadrants (deleted/alive x has/missing deletedBy).

## Key Files
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` - predicate definition beside the delete/attribution logic
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - re-export from the package entry point
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` - quadrant unit tests
